survivingClaim: No statement about zeros of zeta. Relative to the recalled rank-2 Langlands inner product formula (checked for M = 1 against the direct integral): Gram positivity of truncated minimal-parabolic SL3 Eisenstein series is not closed under Blaschke insertion. A zero of M with 0 < Re a < 1/2 forces a zero at 1 - a (Lemma R, confirmed, valid for a general simple pole p). Measured in addition by this referee: an odd number of real inserted zeros (other than a single zero at 1) fails. Symmetric insertions (zeta times a symmetric polynomial) and non-real conjugate pairs right of 1/2 pass at every tested T >= 0. This is MEASURED twice on different samples (lane: about 4,700 matrices of order up to 5; referee: order-7 matrices plus 3,960 residue-form values per case along the three polar divisors, 0 negative); closure is not proved. DH passes on 400 low-height diagonals and is not shown to fail. At a hypothetical off-line pair, form (*) is confirmed: Q(eta, t_2) is height-independent and positive on a 99 x 34 grid for t_2 >= 0, so it gives no contradiction. Verdict precise-obstruction with a device row stands, with the BLS-right row restricted as above.

lesson: Rank 2 adds one condition to rank one: left-half zeros of the scattering coefficient must be reflected, which is the functional equation of the zero set. Reading f(z) = f(1-z) or the exact normalisation does not leave the Blaschke control: its symmetric form is zeta times a symmetric polynomial and stays positive on a larger set of T than zeta. The BLS control row's "lacks f(z) = f(1-z)" is wrong for symmetric zero sets.
followUp: Prove or refute closure of the rank-2 Gram form under symmetric and right-unpaired Blaschke factors; cheap first step is a larger adversarial search on the server (order 10 to 20, zero heights to 1e3). Also owed: an independent referee, and a source check of the inner product formula and the valid range of T.
